subject: chem
title: Equilibrium
syllabus: Meaning of equilibrium, the concept of dynamic equilibrium. Equilibria involving physical processes: Solid-liquid, liquid-gas and solid-gas equilibria, Henry's law. General characteristics of equilibrium involving physical processes. Equilibrium involving chemical processes: Law of chemical equilibrium, equilibrium constants (Kp and Kc) and their significance, the significance of ΔG and ΔG° in chemical equilibrium, factors affecting equilibrium concentration, pressure, temperature, the effect of catalyst; Le Chatelier's principle. Ionic equilibrium: Weak and strong electrolytes, ionization of electrolytes, various concepts of acids and bases (Arrhenius, Bronsted – Lowry and Lewis) and their ionization, acid-base equilibria (including multistage ionization) and ionization constants, ionization of water, pH scale, common ion effect, hydrolysis of salts and pH of their solutions, the solubility of sparingly soluble salts and solubility products, buffer solutions.

body: At equilibrium the forward and backward rates are equal — both reactions still run (dynamic equilibrium).
aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD: K_{c} = \f{[C]^{c}[D]^{d}}{[A]^{a}[B]^{b}}, K_{p} = K_{c}(RT)^{Δn_{gas}}
Pure solids and liquids are left out of K. Reverse the equation → \f{1}{K}; multiply it by n → K^{n}; add equations → multiply the K values.
K depends ONLY on temperature — not on amounts, pressure or a catalyst.

body: ΔG° = −RT ln K = −2.303RT log K; ΔG = ΔG° + RT ln Q
K > 1 ⇔ ΔG° < 0. At equilibrium ΔG = 0 and Q = K.
A plot of log K vs \f{1}{T} is a straight line of slope −\f{ΔH°}{2.303R}.

body: Disturb an equilibrium and it shifts to undo the change.
Add reactant / remove product → forward. Raise pressure → side with fewer gas moles. Heat → endothermic side (K changes!).
Inert gas at constant volume: no shift. Inert gas at constant pressure: acts like a volume increase → side with more gas moles. Catalyst: no shift, equilibrium is just reached faster.
Q < K → forward, Q > K → backward, Q = K → at equilibrium
Arrhenius (H^{+}/OH^{−}), Brønsted–Lowry (proton donor/acceptor, conjugate pairs), Lewis (electron-pair acceptor/donor).
Weak acid: α ≈ √{\f{K_{a}}{c}}, [H^{+}] ≈ √{K_{a}c}, pH = ½(pK_{a} − log c)
Salts: weak acid + strong base → basic (pH = 7 + ½pK_{a} + ½log c); weak base + strong acid → acidic. Hot water has pH < 7 yet is still neutral.

body: A buffer = weak acid + its salt (or weak base + its salt) in comparable amounts. It resists pH change.
pH = pK_{a} + log\f{[salt]}{[acid]}, pOH = pK_{b} + log\f{[salt]}{[base]}
Half-way through titrating a weak acid, [salt] = [acid] → pH = pK_{a}.
Adding strong acid: turn that many moles of base into salt, then reuse the formula. Blood is buffered by H_{2}CO_{3}/HCO_{3}^{−}.

body: A_{x}B_{y} ⇌ xA^{y+} + yB^{x−}: K_{sp} = (xs)^{x}(ys)^{y} = x^{x}y^{y}s^{x + y}
Ionic product Q > K_{sp} → precipitate. Remember that mixing equal volumes halves each concentration.
Common ion effect: solubility falls sharply, s ≈ \f{K_{sp}}{[common ion]^{n}}. Group separation with H_{2}S works by setting [S^{2−}] with pH.

traps: K changes only with temperature — never with pressure, amounts or a catalyst.
Leave solids and pure liquids out of K (CaCO₃ ⇌ CaO + CO₂ → K_p = p_CO₂).
Inert gas at constant VOLUME does nothing; at constant PRESSURE it shifts towards more gas moles.
Mixing equal volumes halves every concentration before you compare Q with K_sp.
For very dilute or very weak acids, include water's own H⁺ (10⁻⁷ M) — pH of 10⁻⁸ M HCl is not 8.
Heated pure water has pH < 7 but is still neutral.

words: Equilibrium
State where forward and backward rates are equal
Catalyst
Speeds a reaction without shifting equilibrium
Buffer
Solution that resists change in pH
Solubility
Maximum amount that dissolves at a temperature
Hydrolysis
Reaction of a salt ion with water
Conjugate
Acid–base pair differing by one proton
Ionisation
Splitting of a molecule into ions in water
Quotient
Q — same expression as K but at any moment
Dissociation
Breaking of a molecule into smaller parts
Precipitate
Solid that forms when ionic product exceeds Ksp
